auditor: independent AI auditor (did not write the paper); a fresh one for every round

audits.summary: Every number in the paper traces to logged runs and generated tables; the code implements the described method with no test leakage or hard-coded results, and the claims and limitations are stated honestly, including the mixed 25%-density result. Remaining issues are minor: a broken table reference ("??"), one overstated null result in H3, undisclosed TransE run-to-run nondeterminism (~0.01 MRR), and one imprecisely used citation.

findings.issue: \ref{tab:rel.} has a stray period and renders as 'Table ??' in main.pdf.

'the inductive handicap of TransE vanishes' and 'an artefact of the evaluation set-up' read a non-significant difference (-0.012, p=0.59, 5 seeds) as equivalence, against the paper's own rule; fold-in is also test-time training, a different setting.
findings.fix: Say fold-in inductive MRR is not distinguishable from transductive TransE with five seeds, and that fold-in changes the setting by training on the new graph.

findings.where: method/run.py TransE / paper setup 'A seed fixes ...'
findings.issue: TransE is not deterministic run to run: a rerun of seed 3 gave 0.6078/0.6084 against 0.6169 in the registry, and transe vs transe_foldin transductive (identical code) differ by up to 0.018 per seed. The paper implies full determinism.
findings.fix: State the run-to-run variation of TransE (about 0.01 MRR, below the seed std) or make training deterministic.

findings.issue: The 'TransE+fold-in' transductive row is the same code path as TransE (no fold-in happens in that setting), but it is presented as a separate result without explanation.
findings.fix: Note in the caption that fold-in equals TransE transductively, or drop that row.

findings.issue: Rossi et al. is cited for 'classic models are competitive once hyperparameters and training are tuned'; that paper is about design choices and evaluation bias, and the claim belongs to Ruffinelli et al. 2020.
findings.fix: Rephrase to what Rossi et al. show, or cite Ruffinelli et al. (ICLR 2020) for the tuning claim.

findings.issue: 'a standard way to embed out-of-sample entities' has no citation.
findings.fix: Add a citation or soften the wording.

findings.issue: The repository URL overflows past the page edge; the Bordes et al. reference has no venue.
findings.fix: Wrap or shorten the URL with \url line breaks; add the NeurIPS 2013 venue to the bib entry.

pre_submission_reviews.what: Before submission the venue's own review panel (same reviewers, rubric and decision rule as the official round; no area chair) read the study. A study the panel would not accept gets up to two improve rounds, each audited again, and is held back (not submitted) if the panel still would not accept. Papers submitted before 2026-10-03 had no such step.
